summary: A federal jury convicted the club's owner of sex trafficking conspiracy, bribery, conspiracy to defraud the United States, drug conspiracy, maintaining a drug-involved premises and witness tampering.
The owner was sentenced to 25 years in prison. The release says he ran the club from 2005 to 2019.

A federal indictment charged the owner, a manager and a bouncer with conspiring to promote prostitution and illegally employing noncitizens, plus tax, money-laundering and loan-fraud counts against the owner.
The bouncer, who mainly hired the dancers, pleaded guilty to conspiring to promote prostitution.
The former owner pleaded guilty to conspiring to promote prostitution, a tax conspiracy and money-laundering counts. The release says the club ran from the 1990s until it was sold in January 2025.
The former owner was sentenced to 16 months in prison, with about $1.5 million forfeited and restitution ordered to the IRS and the SBA.

Seven people were indicted in an interstate prostitution and sex trafficking business, including trafficking of a 17-year-old. The lead defendant was named as a part owner of the club, which the release says had closed.
A man who began working for the business's leader at the club in 2012 pleaded guilty to conspiracy.
The Lawrence nightclub owner charged as the business's leader pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit sex trafficking by force, fraud or coercion.
A jury convicted the man who ran a strip club and brothel at a leased property in Philadelphia of sex trafficking by force and attempted sex trafficking. A security worker was also convicted.
The operator of Club Passions and the brothel beside it, Passionate Touch, was sentenced to 100 years in prison.

The couple who ran Goodfellas were sentenced for interstate prostitution offenses, one to a year and a day in prison and the other to probation. The release says the club advertised exotic dancers but was run as a prostitution business from at least 2003 to October 2013.

Two owners of this bar and La Hija del Mariachi, and a manager of both, were arrested on sex trafficking, forced labor and harboring charges. Women, some said to be 17, were allegedly lured to work as waitresses and hostesses.
After a jury trial, the bars' owner was sentenced to 60 years for sex trafficking, forced labor and immigration crimes. Two co-defendants got 25 and 30 years.

Two owners of this bar and Sonidos de la Frontera, and a manager of both, were arrested on sex trafficking, forced labor and harboring charges. Women, some said to be 17, were allegedly lured to work as waitresses and hostesses.
After a jury trial, the bars' owner was sentenced to 60 years for sex trafficking, forced labor and immigration crimes. Two co-defendants got 25 and 30 years.

A man was sentenced to 27 years for sex trafficking by force, fraud and coercion. He recruited women and at least one minor and took them to strip clubs including TNT and the Hardware Store. The release doesn't say club staff took part.
The club's owner and a former manager were indicted on a 2012 to 2019 conspiracy to promote prostitution. The owner also faced false tax return counts for Tequila Nights, Inc.
A grand jury indicted a club owner and a former bartender and manager of The Hardware Store on a 2009 to 2018 conspiracy to promote prostitution.

A man was sentenced to 27 years for sex trafficking by force, fraud and coercion. He recruited women and at least one minor and took them to strip clubs including TNT and the Hardware Store. The release doesn't say club staff took part.

Three men were sentenced to 210, 120 and 34 months for sex trafficking and related crimes. They brought women from Cuba, held smuggling debts over them, and made them dance and sell sex at Houston-area clubs including Michael's International. The release doesn't say the club was charged.

The owner was found guilty of racketeering, racketeering conspiracy, cocaine trafficking and money laundering. A Tampa police undercover probe found drug sales by dancers and staff and offers of sex for money. The release calls it a drug and human trafficking ring, but lists no trafficking or prostitution count.

After allegations that the club let a minor, said to be controlled by a suspected trafficker, work as a dancer, the club agreed to permanent cancellation of its liquor permit. TABC's grounds were human trafficking, employment harmful to a child and drug sales.

A man who recruited at least three minors and two young women to work at strip clubs in San Antonio, Houston and Travis County was convicted of human trafficking and aggravated promotion of prostitution and sentenced to 35 years. Blush is the one club the release names.
The person who ran the cantina pleaded guilty to sex trafficking conspiracy, sex trafficking by force, fraud or coercion, and sex trafficking of a minor. Victims were forced into sex in back rooms.

The operator was sentenced to 280 months and an enforcer to 180 months. Women hired as waitresses were forced into sex in hidden back rooms from 2015 to 2020, and a minor was trafficked. The liquor license holder and a relative were also convicted.

TABC and county officials arrested the bar's owner and her son after reports that young women were recruited and forced to work there. The owner was indicted on trafficking and sexual assault counts, including of a child, and TABC cancelled the bar's permit.

The owner was sentenced to 360 months and her son to 72 months for sex trafficking. Women and girls smuggled from Mexico, one aged 12, were forced into sex with customers. The court ordered the bar and the owner's home forfeited.

The leader of a 14-defendant sex trafficking ring run out of the cantina was sentenced to life after a 2015 jury verdict. Many victims were underage, some recruited at 14. Fifteen properties were forfeited.

A jury convicted the bar's owner of sex trafficking and harboring; he was later sentenced to 360 months. Agents rescued three girls, aged 14, 15 and 17, who had been smuggled from Honduras and prostituted at the bar.
A federal jury in Guam convicted the lounge's owner on all 20 counts. About nine women recruited from Chuuk were forced into sex in the bar's VIP rooms.
The owner was sentenced to life in prison, with $200,000 restitution, on counts including sex trafficking and transporting a minor for prostitution.
A federal jury convicted the club's owner of sex trafficking by force, fraud or coercion for conduct from 2008 to 2009.
The owner was sentenced to 235 months for forcing a woman he recruited into sex with customers, using her debt and immigration status.

A 12-count indictment charged the room salon's owner, managers and others with transporting women for prostitution, money laundering, visa fraud, harboring and bribery. Hostesses allegedly had to repay their travel costs.
The owner pleaded guilty to conspiring to transport people for prostitution, money laundering conspiracy, bribing a state liquor board investigator and tax evasion, and was sentenced to 72 months.
The state ABC Director revoked the club's liquor permits. The charges included entertainers soliciting prostitution, simulated sex acts, contact with customers and drugs on the premises.
On appeal, the ABC Board adopted findings on most charges and set a $40,000 fine, then voted 3 to 2 to stay the revocation.
The Arkansas Court of Appeals upheld the revocation of the club's two liquor permits, based on 34 violations including four solicitation charges.

TABC found evidence of prostitution and drink solicitation by ficheras, women paid to spend time with customers. The owners agreed to surrender the license, and the bar was cited for allowing prostitution.

After an investigation that began on tips about organized crime including human trafficking, the owner surrendered the liquor license. TABC charged the bar with drink solicitation, prostitution and drug sales by an employee, and referred possible trafficking victims for help.

A March 2022 prostitution and human trafficking investigation found a suspected brothel at the bar. TABC ordered a 90-day stop to alcohol sales, then permanently cancelled the license. Criminal charges against several people were allegations when announced.

After a month-long operation with the Travis County Sheriff's Office and federal partners, TABC cancelled the bar's liquor permit, citing narcotics, drink solicitation and human trafficking. These were allegations, and the investigation was still open.

The City of El Paso sued for injunctions against the club, citing more than 25 alleged violations including prostitution, drug dealing, sexual assault and sexual exploitation. A separate county order shut the club until March 5, 2024. Allegations.

In an agreed order, without admitting the nuisance claims, the defendants agreed the club can't operate as Jaguars Gold Club or as a sexually oriented business, posted a $5,000 bond and accepted other conditions.

The county told the court that Chicas Locas held a grand opening at the same address on Sept. 19, 2024, with Jaguars signs still up, and asked it to forfeit the bond and close the site for a year. Allegations; we haven't found a ruling.
The appeals court's opinion says the club kept operating without a license after an October 2020 order to shut down, and that it can't get a sexually oriented business permit at this location.

The Fourteenth Court of Appeals upheld a City of Houston nuisance injunction against the operator, the landlord and the property, including full closure if it's violated. The opinion cites a 2021 prostitution arrest of an entertainer, underage entertainers found in 2021 and a manager's arrest for employing a minor.

The Fourteenth Court of Appeals upheld a temporary nuisance injunction sought by the State and the City of Houston. The trial court had found the club habitually used for prostitution and drug activity and that it knowingly tolerated it. The injunction set rules such as bag checks, dress rules and cameras rather than closing the club.

The club's owner was arrested on a charge of aggravated promotion of prostitution, accused of offering to supply women for sex for money, and a manager on a charge of selling alcohol without a permit. Four women got victim services. Charges, not convictions.
The El Paso County Attorney's Office shut the club down, to stay closed until a temporary injunction hearing set for June 24, 2021.

An investigation begun on complaints of possible human trafficking found evidence of drug trafficking, prostitution and drink solicitation. An emergency order suspended the permit for 90 days. Allegations.

A federal complaint charges the club's owner, a manager and a driver with conspiring to transport people for prostitution, travel in aid of racketeering and harboring noncitizens. It alleges the club ran as a brothel with a fee scheme that pressured dancers. Allegations.

A federal court order describes the Providence Board of Licenses revoking the club's licenses after finding that the licensee's gross negligence allowed two prostitution incidents and a cocaine sale. The court refused to block the revocation.
